title: Arrival at Jezero
objective: Get your bearings at the landing site.

objectives.label: Look around from the landing panorama

discovery: Jezero held a lake. Its delta is the reason the rover is here, though the rocks under your feet at the landing site turned out not to be lake sediment at all.

title: The Crater Floor
location: Máaz formation, south of the landing site
objective: Head south along the edge of Séítah to the Citadelle ridge.

objectives.label: Inspect Roubion, the first coring attempt

discovery: The crater floor is igneous rock altered by water. Because igneous rock can be dated, these cores could give Jezero's history real ages once they are on Earth.

title: Into Séítah
objective: Enter the dune-filled Séítah region and reach its layered outcrops.
discovery: Séítah is an olivine cumulate: crystals that settled out of slowly cooling magma. It later reacted with water to form carbonate. Organic molecules were detected in crater-floor rocks, which is not the same as detecting life.

title: Closing the Crater Floor
location: Adziilii crater and Sid, near the landing site
objective: Retrace the route north and collect the last crater-floor cores.

objectives.label: View the Sid and Ch'ał rocks panorama

discovery: Eight rock cores now span the crater floor's igneous history. The sediment the lake left behind lies ahead, at the delta.

title: The Delta Front
objective: Explore the exposed delta-front layers at Rockytop Scarp.
discovery: The delta front holds lake mud and river sand. The Wildcat Ridge mudstone carries organic molecules alongside sulfate salts: a habitable setting and a strong sample, but not evidence of life.

title: The Sample Depot
objective: Visit the flat ground where the rover left its backup samples.
discovery: Ten tubes lie at Three Forks: a complete, documented sample set waiting on the surface of another planet.

title: Fan Top and Margin
location: Upper fan and the crater's inner margin
campaign: Upper Fan and Margin Unit Campaigns
objective: Climb onto the delta and follow its top west to the carbonate-bearing margin.
discovery: Boulders on the fan top record violent late floods. The margin's carbonates formed with water, but whether on a lake shore or underground is still argued.

title: Neretva Vallis and Bright Angel
objective: Drop into the dry river channel and reach the pale outcrop on its far bank.
discovery: Cheyava Falls contains organic carbon and mineral 'leopard spots' that could be a trace of ancient microbes or of non-living chemistry. It is a potential biosignature and remains unresolved.

title: The Crater Rim
location: Western rim: Lookout Hill, Witch Hazel Hill, Krokodillen
objective: Climb out of the crater to the rim crest and explore its outer slope.

objectives.label: View the rim crest at Lookout Hill
Inspect the Silver Mountain core site

discovery: You are standing on rock far older than the lake. Rim samples such as Silver Mountain may record what early Mars' crust was like.

title: Beyond the Rim
location: Crocodile Bridge and Lac de Charmes
objective: Follow the rover west, out of Jezero.
discovery: You have caught up with the rover. What these rocks mean is being worked out now.
